compatibility.title: Which Models Use the FA20?
compatibility.intro: The FA20 was developed specifically for the Subaru BRZ and Toyota GT86 (also sold as the Scion FR-S in North America). It is a joint development between Subaru and Toyota, combining Subaru's boxer engine architecture with Toyota's D-4S fuel injection technology. The turbocharged FA20F/FA20DIT variant was also used in the Subaru Forester XT, Legacy, Levorg and WRX.

failures.title: Subaru FA20 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails
failures.goodYearsLine: The FA20 improved over its production run. The valve spring recall affected 2012-2013 models; post-2015 cars are generally considered more sorted. The second-generation BRZ/GR86 (2022+) uses the larger FA24 engine with a revised oil system. The FA20 remains a reliable engine for road use, but track use requires oil system upgrades.

variants.title: FA20 Variants - Which One Is in Your Car?
variants.intro: INTRO: The FA20 family includes both naturally aspirated and turbocharged variants. The naturally aspirated FA20D (also called 4U-GSE by Toyota) is the engine in the BRZ and GT86. The turbocharged FA20F (also called FA20DIT) is found in the WRX, Forester XT, Legacy and Levorg. These are NOT interchangeable. ### FA20D / 4U-GSE - 2012-2021 (naturally aspirated, BRZ/GT86) - Fitted to: Subaru BRZ (ZC, 2012-2021), Toyota GT86 (ZN6, 2012-2021), Scion FR-S (2012-2016) - Key technical difference: Naturally aspirated, DOHC, 16-valve. Toyota D-4S fuel system combining direct and port injection. Compression ratio: 12.5:1. Bore and stroke: 86.0 mm × 86.0 mm (square). Redline: 7,450 rpm. Power: 200 hp (147 kW) at 7,000 rpm; torque: 205 Nm at 6,400-6,600 rpm. Dual AVCS (Subaru) / Dual VVT-i (Toyota) variable valve timing. Timing chain driven. Weight: 170 kg. Recommended oil: 0W-20. Oil capacity: 6.3 litres. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Oil pressure loss in high-G right-hand turns is the primary concern. Valve spring recall affected 2012-2013 production. Carbon buildup can occur despite D-4S dual injection. - Interchange note: Not interchangeable with FA20F - the turbo variant has different internals, lower compression (10.6:1), different ECU, and different ancillaries. Ensure your replacement matches your engine type. ### FA20F / FA20DIT - 2012-2021 (turbocharged, WRX/Forester XT) - Fitted to: Subaru Forester XT (SJ, 2013-2018), Subaru Legacy (BM/BN, 2012-2019), Subaru Levorg (VM, 2014-2020), Subaru WRX (VA, 2014-2021) - Key technical difference: Turbocharged, DOHC, 16-valve. Direct injection only. Compression ratio: 10.6:1 (lower than FA20D). Twin-scroll turbocharger with intercooler. Power output: 250-300 hp depending on tune. Torque: 350-400 Nm. Recommended oil: 5W-30. Oil capacity: 5.1 litres. Weight: 185 kg. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Timing chain rattle on cold start is more commonly reported. Oil temperature management is a concern under sustained load. Carbon buildup on intake valves. - Interchange note: Not interchangeable with FA20D - compression ratio, internals, turbo, intercooler, ECU, and wiring loom are all different. Only replace with another FA20F.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement FA20 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used FA20 from a BRZ/GT86 makes sense if it comes with documented service history, has had the valve spring recall completed (if applicable), and preferably has evidence of a recent oil pressure system check. However, used FA20s are often from cars that have been driven hard - track use without oil system upgrades can lead to bearing wear. A compression test and oil pressure test are essential before purchase. Used FA20F turbo engines should be treated with even more caution - oil starvation and turbo failure are common on modified cars.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper FA20 recon addresses the known weak points: for FA20D, new bearings, improved oil pickup (to address oil starvation), new timing chain tensioner, and a thorough carbon clean of intake valves. A 12-month warranty is standard. Reconditioned units are the sweet spot for most owners - you get the reliability upgrades without the cost of a full rebuild.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full FA20 rebuild is justified when you own a cherished BRZ/GT86 and want the engine to last another 100,000+ miles - particularly if you track the car. An upgraded rebuild should include forged pistons and rods (especially if you plan to supercharge or turbocharge later), ARP head studs, a baffled oil pan, and an upgraded oil pickup. Budget £4,500-£6,500 for a quality rebuild. For track use, consider adding an oil cooler and Accusump system.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: All of our vetted UK Subaru and Toyota specialists offer supply-only or full supply-and-fit - nationwide delivery and recovery available, with warranties that cover both parts and labour.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The FA20 sits in affordable sports cars - BRZ/GT86 values range from £6,000-£18,000 depending on year, mileage and condition. A reconditioned FA20 at £2,800-£4,200 represents 15-50% of vehicle value - generally viable for most examples. However, for a high-mileage (£5,000-£8,000) early BRZ/GT86, a full rebuild at £6,500 may approach or exceed the vehicle's value. In those cases, evaluate the car's overall condition, rust, and chassis health before committing. A clean, low-mileage example justifies the spend; a tired car may be better broken for parts .

items.question: What are the most common FA20 engine problems?
items.answer: The FA20 suffers from oil pressure loss and bearing failure (especially during track use / high-G corners), a valve spring recall (2012-2013 models), carbon buildup on intake valves, and timing chain rattle on cold starts. Oil system upgrades (baffled pan, improved pickup) cost £500-£1,000. Valve spring recall is free if not already completed. Carbon cleaning costs £300-£600.

items.question: Which models use the FA20 engine?
items.answer: The naturally aspirated FA20D (4U-GSE) is fitted to the Subaru BRZ (2012-2021), Toyota GT86 (2012-2021), and Scion FR-S (2012-2016). The turbocharged FA20F/FA20DIT is fitted to the Subaru Forester XT, Legacy, Levorg, and WRX. These are completely different engines and are NOT interchangeable.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned FA20?
items.answer: A reconditioned FA20 is the safer choice - it includes improved bearings, an oil pickup upgrade (to address oil starvation), and a 12-month warranty. Used FA20s are only recommended if they have documented service history and the valve spring recall completed. Track-used cars without oil system upgrades are high-risk purchases.

items.question: What's the difference between FA20 and FA20F?
items.answer: The FA20D is the naturally aspirated version (BRZ/GT86) with 12.5:1 compression and 200 hp. The FA20F is the turbocharged version (WRX/Forester XT) with 10.6:1 compression, a twin-scroll turbo, and 250-300 hp. They are NOT interchangeable - different internals, ECU, wiring, and ancillaries. Only buy an engine that matches your model.
bullets: They are NOT interchangeable - different internals, ECU, wiring, and ancillaries.
Only buy an engine that matches your model.

items.question: How long does an FA20 engine last?
items.answer: With regular maintenance (oil changes every 5k-6k miles using 0W-20 for NA or 5W-30 for turbo), an FA20 can exceed 150,000 miles. Oil starvation is the main limit on track-used cars. Carbon buildup requires periodic cleaning. The valve spring recall is critical - ensure it's completed.
